stem:
Vivaan's class asks why the Southern Hemisphere has summer in December while the Northern Hemisphere has winter then.

Answer both parts.

options.text: Earth's tilted axis stays pointed the same way as Earth revolves, so in December the Southern Hemisphere gets more direct sunlight and longer days.
In December the Southern Hemisphere has summer because its tilt brings it closer to the Sun.
In December both hemispheres have summer.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The maintained tilt makes one hemisphere lean toward the Sun at a time, so December gives the Southern Hemisphere more direct sunlight and longer days, not a closer orbit.

teacher.key_rationale: Seasons come from Earth's maintained axial tilt during revolution, which changes sunlight intensity and day length by hemisphere. Closer-to-Sun tilt and both-hemispheres-summer are wrong.
